messages:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a clear latency regression on sm88 for long-seq INT4 paths after yesterday's autotune rollout. baseline vs current is ~+40% tail.

mira: Which model and input shape?

alex: gpt-medium (llama-variant), seq_len=2048, batch=1. Autotuner is choosing an INT4 kernel initially then flipping to an FP8-backed kernel during KV warmup which spikes latency. Repro here on a dedicated SM88 node.

devon: Can you paste the quick profile snippet you captured?

alex: sure — minimal excerpt from perf profiler run: 
```
PROFILE sm88 gpt-medium seq=2048 batch=1
selected_quant=INT4 -> chosen_kernel=kv_attn_v2_int4_sm88 (initial)
observed_warmup: applied_fp8_kernel_for_first_8_steps (flip)
step_times(ms): attn=9.4, kv_copy=2.1, matmul=13.2, total_token=29.7
baseline(prev): attn=6.7, matmul=10.1, total=23.0
kernel_switch_point: token=8
```

mira: Interesting. The autotuner change yesterday reduced seq_threshold from 1024->512 to favor int4 for mid lengths. That could explain more aggressive switching.

nora: I can confirm the rollout — seq_threshold was lowered to 512 to improve perf for 512-1024 workloads. Didn't think about long-seq KV warmup interactions.

sam: That was my change — aimed at improving median latency for 768/1024 loads. Oops if it's causing regressions for >1024.

devon: Two hypotheses: 1) seq_threshold change causes initial kernel pick to prefer INT4 but KV warmup triggers an FP8 fallback due to numeric stability heuristics, 2) hysteresis is too small so we flip back-and-forth during early tokens.

alex: We see a single flip at token 8, after which FP8 path stays active for the rest of the request, and FP8 is slower for this model/hardware combo at batch=1.

mira: Short-term mitigations: revert seq_threshold to 1024 for sm88 only, or add a KV-aware condition to prevent kernel switches while kv_warmup_steps < X.

devon: Suggest we add two params to autotuner: `seq_switch_threshold` (per-arch override) and `quant_switch_hysteresis` (min_stable_tokens). Also `min_batch_for_quant` to avoid aggressive quant picks on batch=1.

alex: +1. Also want a tracing field emitted: selected_quant_reason (eg "autotune(seq=2048, kv_warmup=8)") so we can search logs.

sam: Repro script lives at ci/artifacts/sm88/1803001234/repro.sh (link posted). I ran it with docker and got same numbers.

perf-bot: CI run #4221 detected: p50 latency unchanged, p95 increased beyond threshold for sm88-longseq-int4 profile — failing with 1.42x compared to baseline. Full logs: https://ci.redwood/internal/4221/logs

nora: For immediate rollback I can push a per-arch flag to revert seq_threshold only on sm88. That avoids global revert. Thoughts?

devon: That's safest. Put a short TTL (24h) while we implement hysteresis and min_batch guards. I'll add automated alert if kernel_switch_count/request > 1 for the same trace.

mira: I'll add trace fields and a sampling rule to capture long-seq requests (seq>=1536) for deeper analysis.

alex: I'll open PRs: 1) revert-sm88-seq-threshold (urgent), 2) autotune-hysteresis-rfc (design) — assign reviewers devon/mira.

sam: Thanks — if you want I can run a small canary after revert on the dedicated pool. :thumbsup: 

alex: sweet. Filing the PRs now, will tag the rollout channel when canary completes.
